title: The Future of Drone Warfare

reader_summary.headline: The industrial capacity of China is fearsome.
reader_summary.overview: The industrial capacity of China is fearsome. Being able to deploy highly autonomous AI-driven drones at scale is still a domain that we can win in. I think the technologies that matter most of the future of war are right there and front of us.

key_points.text: Living a modern conflict becomes basically like a software writing fight.
key_points.evidence_quote: Living a modern conflict becomes basically like a software writing fight.

key_points.text: It will be the pace of deployment that is the make or break for militaries around the world.

key_points.text: The game theory here is just as simple and obvious as it can be.
key_points.evidence_quote: The game theory here is just as simple and obvious as it can be.

key_points.text: Unless we find a way for industry and government to work together, we will find ourselves in a very tough situation.

thesis: The episode argues that the future of warfare is already here, defined by AI-empowered drones that provide asymmetric capabilities where low-cost units can disable high-value equipment. It posits that the decisive factor for militaries will be the pace of deployment and the ability of industry and government to collaborate, noting that China currently dominates about 80% of the global drone market.
